<!-- Issues are public, they should not contain confidential information -->

### Problem to solve
<!-- It should respond to why the feature is needed and what problem it aims
to solve. The origin of the problem should be clarified -->

### Solution
<!-- A concise summary of the solution (2-4 sentences) before diving into
details. Explains the approach from the user's perspective. -->

### User Stories
<!-- A numbered list of user stories in the format:
1. As an <actor>, I want a <feature>, so that <benefit>
This list should be extensive and cover all aspects of the feature. -->

### Acceptance criteria
<!-- A checklist of verifiable conditions that must all be true for this
issue to be considered done. Frame each as end-to-end behavior, not a
layer-by-layer implementation detail. Format:
- [ ] Criterion -->

### Intended users
<!-- It should clarify who will benefit from the feature, and how it will
be used. -->

### Proposal
<!-- It should clarify the proposed solution, and how it addresses the problem.
A step by step plan must be included here. Include:
- Architecture and module structure
- Specific implementation decisions (schemas, API contracts, interactions)
- Technical clarifications and edge cases -->

### Test plan
<!-- Business related test cases and edge cases. Include:
- A description of what makes a good test for this feature
- Which modules will be tested
- Prior art (similar tests in the codebase to reference) -->

### Steps


### What does success look like, and how can we measure that?

<!-- MANDATORY

### Out of Scope
<!-- What is explicitly not included in this issue. Helps prevent scope creep
and sets clear boundaries for implementation. -->

### Further Notes
<!-- Design rationale, additional context, or notes that don't fit
elsewhere. -->
